rows.label: Do Not Disturb
rows.help: Stays on screen, silences sounds, stops initiating actions.
rows.disclosure: Do Not Disturb leaves the fidget visible but quiet: proposals are refused and unprompted dialogue is not spoken. Poke, Grab, and Throw still work. The Cue (visual + sound) acknowledges each interaction. This switch silences the sound and keeps the visual.

rows.label: Sound
rows.help: Off silences audio cues.
rows.disclosure: A synthesized sound accompanies each Cue. This switch silences them. Do Not Disturb (above) takes the sound with it.

rows.label: Go away
rows.help: Go off screen. But still exist.

rows.label: Hide in fullscreen apps
rows.help: Steps aside for fullscreen apps.

rows.label: Appear in screenshots and screen shares
rows.help: Checked: visible in captures. Linux has no exclusion API (always visible). Needs restart.

rows.label: Hide/Show Toggle
rows.help: Hides or shows from any app.

rows.label: Launch at login (unimplemented)
rows.help: Not available yet.
The character your fidget wears. Read from /Users/buddy/Library/Application Support/fidget/characters.
rows.disclosure: Characters are packages: art, personality, and behaviors bundled together. Two ship with the app.

rows.help: Fidgets on screen now.
rows.disclosure: An Instance is one spawned fidget: a Character plus a user-given name and a stable id. Instances share Memory, and differ in personality (Instance Prompt) and behavior, never in what they know.

rows.help: Adds another fidget.

sections.heading: AI

rows.label: AI on
rows.help: Lets the model pick what happens next.
rows.disclosure: With this off, the fidget runs on static weights: predefined behaviors chosen by their declared weights, no model involved. With it on and no Harness attached, the HTTP endpoint (base URL, model, and key below) proposes behaviors and short lines. With it on and a Harness attached that answers, that Harness is the "AI brain" for every Instance.

rows.label: Proactive model calls
rows.help: Acts on its own, not only when asked.
rows.disclosure: Proactive model calls address you after being idle long enough, on an exponential backoff. With this off, wakes are reactive only — you have to address it first. The switch below sets how long the first one waits.

rows.help: Throws the conversation in flight away and opens a fresh one.
rows.disclosure: Every other row stays where it is: the same AI source, the same model and key, the same Blank AI, the same Character and Instance Prompt. What goes is the conversation — the turns held here, and the history, tool results, and files the AI brain was holding for this fidget. The next wake is an opening turn rather than a follow-up. Memory is untouched.

sections.comment: Control whether the fidget improvises, and how often it starts a conversation on its own.
sections.disclosure: The fidget can run on static weights (no model calls) or with a Model API (the HTTP endpoint below, or an attached Harness). AI on with no Harness uses the HTTP endpoint. An attached Harness that answers becomes the "AI brain".

sections.heading: AI source

rows.label: AI source
rows.help: Which "AI brain" answers for the fidget.
rows.disclosure: Model API: the HTTP endpoint below. Harness · {name}: starts that Harness and makes it the AI brain. Standalone CLIs (copilot, cursor-agent, goose, grok, hermes, opencode) require only their binary on PATH. antigravity requires Google's agy_acp_server on PATH. Registry adapters (claude, codex, pi) also require Node.js and npx. Harness · Custom: the command line below. The line below this row shows what is attached and whether it is signed in. Apply commits the pick.

rows.label: Write .mcp.json in the working directory
rows.status: Apply creates /Users/buddy/Library/Application Support/fidget/.mcp.json, or updates only its Fidget entry. The entry names FIDGET_MCP_URL and FIDGET_MCP_TOKEN. The port and the token stay out of the file, and a later Apply leaves a correct file alone. Pi still needs pi-mcp-adapter, or the file does nothing.

rows.label: Custom command line
rows.disclosure: The command Fidget runs when Custom is picked above. Apply commits it and re-opens the attachment. Cancel restores the line.

rows.help: Harness signs itself in - Fidget never asks for credentials.
rows.disclosure: Fidget holds no credential for the Harness. The Harness authenticates itself, and the login command this line may show is text: nothing here runs it for you. This line shows three states: not attached, attached but not signed in (with the login command), or attached and answering (with a session UUID).

sections.comment: Choose which "AI brain" answers: Model API or an attached Harness.
sections.disclosure: Model API uses the HTTP endpoint below (base URL, model, and key). A Harness (claude, codex, copilot, cursor-agent, goose, grok, hermes, opencode, pi, antigravity, or Custom) attaches a child process and makes it the AI brain, and the HTTP rows stop driving. Standalone binaries (copilot, cursor-agent, goose, grok, hermes, opencode) need only their CLI on PATH. antigravity needs Google's agy_acp_server on PATH. Registry adapters (claude, codex, pi) require Node.js and npx. Apply is the one moment the attachment changes: Cancel restores both rows and leaves the running child alone.

sections.heading: Point a Harness you run yourself at Fidget

rows.label: Harness
rows.help: Preview instructions for this Harness. Apply saves the choice; Cancel restores it.
Good for this app run only. Come back here and copy it again after a relaunch.
rows.disclosure: The port and the token are both new every launch, so a paste from yesterday stops connecting.

rows.help: Paste at Hermes auth prompt; no Bearer prefix; rotates each launch.
This token reaches Fidget and nothing else. The Harness signs itself in.

sections.comment: For a Harness you start in your own terminal.
sections.disclosure: Registering Fidget as an MCP server there lets it speak, move and emote the fidget on your screen. Nothing here changes which mind the Director uses.

rows.help: Fills in the Base URL below. Any other OpenAI-compatible endpoint can be typed there.

rows.label: Model
rows.help: Leave blank to leave the model unset on HTTP and on a Harness. A typed name is sent as the model.
Apply saves AI switches, wake interval, endpoint, AI source, and registration choice.
The last thing sent to the model.
rows.disclosure: This is the Character Prompt (opening turn) or the short follow-up (later wakes), inspectable so you can see exactly what context leaves your machine.

rows.label: UI Theme
rows.help: Visual design for the chat surface.
rows.disclosure: The chat UI is the chat surface's visual design. The overlay, sprite, and speech bubble are unaffected.

rows.label: Light/Dark Mode
rows.help: Light or dark for the Chat surface. System follows this computer.
rows.disclosure: The overlay and speech bubble are unchanged.

rows.label: Trace frames
rows.help: Prints each frame.

sections.disclosure: Development switches print to stderr. Trace frames prints each frame the Engine produces. Trace hit-test prints where each click went (the sprite or click-through). Trace AI prints each model call with its context. Trace Engine prints each change of Behavior or Animation.

sections.heading: Blank AI

rows.label: Blank AI
rows.help: Built-in prompts emptied. An Instance Prompt still goes out.

sections.comment: Also for development and testing. Off is the fidget as shipped.
sections.disclosure: Blank AI empties the built-in Personality Prompt and the app-level instructions (voice rules, behavior list, reply contract). An Instance Prompt you write still goes out, so a control run can iterate a prompt under Fidget's conditions. The Prompt tab shows those three layers; emptied ones say Empty. Without a contract the fidget says what comes back and plays no Behavior unless that Instance Prompt asks for one. Switching it opens a new session, so no session mixes the two prompts.

sections.heading: HTTP limits

rows.label: Timeout, in seconds
rows.help: Model API hop. Expiry falls back to default behavior.

rows.label: Turn ceiling, in tokens
rows.help: A runaway guard, not a reply length. HTTP endpoint only.
Fills in the field below. Any value the server takes can be typed there.

rows.label: Reasoning effort
rows.help: Leave blank to omit effort. A typed value is sent as written to the Completer in use.

sections.comment: Also for development and testing. Leave empty for the default.
sections.disclosure: Timeout is the Model API hop only: an HTTP request, then fallback to default behavior. Leave empty for 30 seconds (the default), remote or local. A Harness turn's timeout is the row under Harness attachment. Turn ceiling is the HTTP endpoint's alone, and it is a safeguard against a model that will not stop rather than a reply length: it does not vary by what woke the fidget or by where the server runs, and an endpoint seen to mark its thinking is given room to think instead. A Harness decides its own reply length. Reasoning effort is one value for the Completer in use. Leave it empty to leave effort unset: HTTP omits the field, and a Harness does not call session/set_config_option. The picker lists low, medium, and high. Other typed values are sent as written. On a Harness the value is set on thought_level, or on model_config if that is what the Harness lists.

sections.heading: Harness attachment

rows.label: Turn timeout, in seconds
rows.help: Harness session/prompt. Expiry cancels the turn.

rows.label: Auth retry, in seconds
rows.help: How long before retrying session/new.

rows.label: MCP server binary
rows.placeholder: beside the app, or this app as its own MCP server
rows.help: The stdio MCP server for the Harness.

rows.label: Working directory
rows.help: The directory the Harness treats as the project, and where it finds the MCP servers you configured for that project. Session file and Action Log stay in the data folder.

sections.comment: Also for development and testing. Leave empty for the default.
sections.disclosure: Turn timeout: how long a session/prompt may run before session/cancel, not counting the time it waits on you to answer an ask, and started over once you answer. Leave empty for 120 seconds (the default). Auth retry: how long a Harness that has not signed in is left alone before session/new is tried again. MCP server binary: the stdio MCP server handed to the Harness session. A path that is not a file falls back to the default (beside the app, or this app as its own MCP server). Working directory: the directory the Harness treats as the project, and where it finds the MCP servers you configured for that project. Session file and Action Log stay in the data folder.
